Lakeview.name: G.E. Booth WRRF (Lakeview)
notes: Rated capacity is the annual average daily influent flow; no peak hydraulic capacity is stated.
Down about 9% from the 2019 peak (91% of capacity), mainly from closing a west-to-east connection on March 12, 2025 (flow redistributed to Clarkson).
Seven secondary bypasses in wet weather (725 ML), the largest April 2–4 (452 ML).
Receives York Region and City of Toronto flows.
About 70 ML/d to be diverted east to west to Clarkson (operational 2027–2028).

Clarkson.name: Clarkson WRRF
notes: Rated capacity is the annual average; no peak capacity is stated.
No bypasses or overflows in 2025; high flows March 16 and April 3.

Inglewood.name: Inglewood WWTP
notes: Rated 243 m³/d annual average; 2025 average 102 m³/d, total 37,274 m³.

inflows.name: York Region inflow
inflows.detail: Humber SPS twin 900 mm forcemains at Hwy 427 and Steeles; 13,180,000 m³/yr annual average

inflows.name: City of Toronto inflow
inflows.detail: three connections into Peel's system; 11,016,000 m³/yr annual average; receiving plant not stated

notes: G.E. Booth and Clarkson serve over 1.58 million customers in Peel plus York Region and City of Toronto flows (G.E. Booth report p. 9).
York and Toronto flows are about 10% of flows in Peel (Collection System report p. 12).

East trunk system → G.E. Booth: east Mississauga and Brampton, parts of Caledon including Bolton; west trunk system → Clarkson: west Mississauga and Brampton, south Caledon (Collection System report p. 11).

diversion.detail: East-to-west diversion of about 70 ML/d from G.E. Booth to Clarkson; operational 2027 (Collection System report) or 2028 (G.E. Booth report)
